note.en: One-shot by Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro (Deep Think effort) in the WorkBuddy coding-agent harness, using the verbatim prompt from cases.json, with no skill, plugin or MCP server invoked and no custom system prompt. The artifact is a single-file, self-contained HTML page (about 46 KB; Three.js r160 via the jsDelivr CDN, everything else inline, no external assets): a procedurally assembled skeleton mechanical watch movement with a perlage mainplate, a mainspring barrel containing a visible coiled spring of about 11 turns and a 34-tooth ratchet, a four-stage train (centre, third, fourth and escape wheels), a Swiss lever escapement whose pallet fork carries two ruby stones, a balance wheel with an 11-turn blued-steel hairspring oscillating at 4 Hz over roughly plus or minus 135 degrees, three Cotes de Geneve bridges with blued screws, ruby jewels in gold settings, luminous hour and minute hands with a 60-tick chapter ring, a blued seconds hand, a slightly domed sapphire crystal, a polished steel case with crown and lugs, and a leather strap; the studio environment map is generated by PMREM from a procedurally built emissive scene, with three-point lighting, ACES tone mapping and a reflective floor. Interaction: custom orbit controls (drag to rotate, wheel to zoom), an exploded view that eases parts apart by layer, hover labels and pick highlighting for 16 part groups, click-to-pin part detail panel, auto-rotate, a movement run toggle, crystal show/hide and a view reset; showcase time runs at 10x real speed, as stated on screen. Headless-browser review (Edge with SwiftShader, WebGL2) with multiple screenshot passes followed generation and fixed these defects: the renderer lacked preserveDrawingBuffer, so headless screenshots could not capture the WebGL buffer during continuous animation (option enabled); the default camera was too close (radius 7.4) and the watch overflowed the frame (moved to 11.6 with adjusted pitch and azimuth); the studio emissive panels and the mainplate were too dark, so polished steel reflected almost black (environment brightness and envMapIntensity raised, the mainplate lightened and made less metallic); the lugs were oversized bright boxes that met the case awkwardly (shrunk, switched to brushed steel, tucked toward the case); and the strap left a visible gap at the lugs (moved closer and lengthened). The exploded view was verified by a forced-state screenshot; hover picking and the click panel are delivered as code but were not exercised with simulated pointer events in the headless environment. The seconds hand and gear train are linked at correct ratios while the showcase runs 10x faster than real time, as noted in the on-screen copy.

note.zh: 在 WorkBuddy（编码智能体 Harness）中以 Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro（深度思考档）一次生成，使用 cases.json 中的提示词原文，全程未调用任何 skill、插件或 MCP，未使用自定义系统提示词。产出为标准 Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Three.js 工程（package.json、index.html、vite.config.ts、tsconfig.json、src/ 四个模块，约 1300 行）：三层木构塔楼内布置漏壶、受水壶、擒纵轮与棘爪、枢轮（八水斗）、齿轮系、浑象天球、浑仪三环、时轮凸轮与报时木人与钟。全部机械运动由内置 2D 刚体物理引擎实时计算（力/力矩积分、齿轮速度约束、销轴约束、棘轮单向锁、凸轮接触惩罚力、水滴刚体粒子与收集质量），不使用手写动画或直接设置位置；镜头与字幕按时间轴编排（属豁免项）。30 秒讲解流程配八段底部字幕（漏壶注水、受水壶积重倾倒、天衡擒纵进一齿、齿轮传动浑象浑仪、凸轮抬臂击钟报时）。音效与环境声全部由 Web Audio 程序化合成（水滴、轮轴吱呀、擒纵滴答、泄水泼溅、撞钟、低频铺底），无音频文件。验证：npm install 后 tsc --noEmit 严格模式零错误，vite build 通过；dist/index.html 经内联插件打包为单文件（约 621 KB）离线可直接运行、无网络依赖。生成后经无头浏览器截图核对并修复：一是构建内联插件把代码中的 $& 当作替换模式导致产物损坏（改为函数式替换）；二是内联脚本未转义闭合标签导致页面把代码当文本渲染（已转义）；三是初版画面偏暗，按截图反馈提高曝光与环境光。如实说明：提示词要求使用 Bun 运行构建，本环境未提供 Bun，改用 npm + vite 完成等效构建验证；本片为线性播放、无互动操作。
note.en: One-shot by Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro (Deep Think effort) in the WorkBuddy coding-agent harness, using the verbatim prompt from cases.json, with no skill, plugin or MCP server invoked and no custom system prompt. The deliverable is a standard Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Three.js project (package.json, index.html, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json and four src modules, about 1300 lines): a three-tier wooden tower housing a header tank, a tipping receiving vessel, an escapement wheel with pawl, a bucket wheel of eight vessels, a gear train, a celestial globe, a three-ring armillary, an hour cam, and a time-announcing figure with a bell. Every mechanical motion is computed in real time by a built-in 2D rigid-body physics engine (force and torque integration, gear velocity constraints, pin constraints, one-way ratchet locking, penalty-force cam contact, and rigid water droplets with collected mass); nothing is hand-keyed or directly positioned. The camera and captions follow a timeline (the exempt categories). The roughly 30-second explanation runs eight bottom captions (header-tank inflow, the vessel growing heavy and tipping, the escapement advancing one tooth, the gear train driving the globe and armillary, the cam raising the figure to strike the bell). All sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API (droplets, wheel creak, escapement ticks, splash, bell, low pads) with no audio files. Verification: after npm install, tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors in strict mode and vite build succeeds; the inline plugin packs dist/index.html into a single file (about 621 KB) that runs offline with no network dependencies. A headless-browser screenshot review fixed: the build inliner treated $& in the code as a replacement pattern and corrupted the output (switched to function replacement); the inlined script did not escape closing tags so the page rendered code as text (now escaped); and the first render was too dark, so exposure and ambient light were raised per screenshot feedback. Disclosed: the prompt asks for Bun as the package manager; this environment has no Bun, so npm + vite provided the equivalent build verification. The film is linear and has no interactive controls.

note.en: One-shot by Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro (Deep Think effort) in the WorkBuddy coding-agent harness, using the verbatim prompt from cases.json, with no skill, plugin or MCP server invoked and no custom system prompt. The deliverable is a Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Three.js project (four src modules for the film, audio, the cue list and the shell, about 1100 lines) in voxel/block-geometry art with no external assets. Total runtime is 310 seconds, within the 360-second cap, adapting the Zhang Beihai assassination of the old-spaceflight establishment from The Three-Body Problem in four acts: a father-and-son dialogue on a snowy night in a study, a station policy meeting over broadcast, a vacuum EVA assassination with a meteorite bullet, and the starship departure epilogue. Camera work includes slow pushes and handheld micro-drift; characters are procedural block figures with a weapon-holding pose, post-hit tumbling drift, muzzle flash and recoil. All spoken content lives in one structured voiceCues list (14 entries, each with exactly the seven fields id, kind, speaker, text, delivery, start, end); subtitles are driven by that list and rendered bottom-centre as 【speaker】text with the cue id shown for post-production dubbing by id. Sound design is fully synthesized with the Web Audio API (radio noise, heartbeat, breathing, low pads, alarm, thrusters) and respects sound physics: no direct gunshot propagates in vacuum, the shot is only a suit-conducted low thump plus a subjective low-frequency impression, and the impact is conducted structure noise. Verification: tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors in strict mode and vite build succeeds, producing an inlined single-file offline bundle (about 616 KB); a headless-browser screenshot checked the first act (study, figures, snowy window, lamp) plus the subtitle and timecode overlays. Disclosed: the full 310 seconds were not watched frame by frame under time limits; acts two to four are judged correct from code review and the first-act render. The prompt suggests Bun; npm + vite provided the equivalent build in this environment.

note.en: One-shot by Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro (Deep Think effort) in the WorkBuddy coding-agent harness, using the verbatim prompt from cases.json, with no skill, plugin or MCP server invoked and no custom system prompt. The deliverable is a Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + three.js project (six src modules, about 1600 lines); models, textures and audio are all procedural with no external assets. The map is a Dust2 blockout of eight connected areas with full collision: T and CT spawns, Long A, the A site, Mid with a passable door gap, Catwalk, B tunnels and the B site. Characters are procedural block figures (separate head, torso, both arms and both legs, weapon-holding pose) with distinguishable CT and T colours. A data-driven weapon table covers the AK-47 (high damage, heavy recoil), the M4A4 (low recoil, high rate of fire), the AWP (one-shot lethal with a right-click scope that narrows the 3D view and raises a 2D scope overlay), the Glock, USP and Desert Eagle sidearms and the knife; hits resolve per zone (head, chest, stomach, arm, leg) with headshots at twice body damage and armour reduction. The first round is a pistol round (default sidearm, no armour). The C4 flow covers carry, drop on death and pickup, plant countdown at the A and B sites, CT defuse (5 s with a helmet, 10 s without) and the full round resolutions (elimination, explosion, defuse, timeout). 5v5 play (the player plus 4 AI teammates against 5 AI opponents) uses grid A* pathfinding, line-of-sight targeting, engagement fire, and advance-to-site plus defuse participation. The HUD has a spread-reactive crosshair, health and armour, dynamic ammo, a killfeed, a persistent minimap (top-down wall outline, both teams, the C4), an AWP scope overlay and spectate-teammate switching. All sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API (distinct AK, M4, AWP, pistol and knife fire plus reload, footsteps, scope, hit, kill, plant, defuse ticks and explosion). Verification: tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors in strict mode and vite build succeeds, producing an inlined single-file offline bundle (about 626 KB); a headless-browser screenshot checked the HUD, minimap and scene render; missing jump physics were added after review and the project rebuilt clean. Three type-level issues (an unused variable, a parameter name and an array type initializer) were fixed after generation. Disclosed: no human playtest session was run under time limits; AI combat and round flow are judged correct from the code paths and first-frame render. The prompt permits iteration; verification here focused on build and screenshot checks.
